paragraphs.text: וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ֩ שֶׁ֨בַע נָשִׁ֜ים בְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֗ד בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לַחְמֵ֣נוּ נֹאכֵ֔ל וְשִׂמְלָתֵ֖נוּ נִלְבָּ֑שׁ רַ֗ק יִקָּרֵ֤א שִׁמְךָ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אֱסֹ֖ף חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying: “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothing; only let us be called by your name — take away our reproach.”
i18n.he: וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ֩ שֶׁ֨בַע נָשִׁ֜ים בְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֗ד בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לַחְמֵ֣נוּ נֹאכֵ֔ל וְשִׂמְלָתֵ֖נוּ נִלְבָּ֑שׁ רַ֗ק יִקָּרֵ֤א שִׁמְךָ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אֱסֹ֖ף חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
The verse closes the oracle against the daughters of Zion (3:16–4:1): the war losses of 3:25 leave seven women to one man (Wildberger, *Isaiah 1–12*, 1991; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19, 2000; Williamson, *Isaiah 1–5*, ICC, 2006). MT marks a closed paragraph (setumah) after it, and the line keeps the received chapter and verse division.

*yiqqārēʾ šimḵā ʿālênû* is literally “let your name be called over us,” the legal formula of ownership and protection (2 Sam 12:28; Isa 63:19), here of marriage. The line gives the idiom’s sense with ASV, “let us be called by your name.” *ʾĕsōp̄ ḥerpāṯēnû* “take away our reproach”: *ḥerpāh* is the public shame of a woman without husband or children, and the same phrase is Rachel’s at Gen 30:23 (central `yosef-double-name-aetiology`, cited, not applied).

paragraphs.translit: wəheḥĕzīqū šebaʿ nāšīm bəʾīš ʾeḥād bayyōm hahūʾ lēʾmōr laḥmēnū nōʾkēl wəśimlātēnū nilbāš raq yiqqārēʾ šimkā ʿālēnū ʾĕsōp ḥerpātēnū (s)

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ צֶ֣מַח יְהוָ֔ה לִצְבִ֖י וּלְכָב֑וֹד וּפְרִ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְגָא֣וֹן וּלְתִפְאֶ֔רֶת לִפְלֵיטַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: In that day the branch of YHWH shall be beauty and glory, and the fruit of the land shall be pride and honor for the survivors of Israel.
i18n.he: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ צֶ֣מַח יְהוָ֔ה לִצְבִ֖י וּלְכָב֑וֹד וּפְרִ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְגָא֣וֹן וּלְתִפְאֶ֔רֶת לִפְלֵיטַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

notes.official:
*ṣemaḥ YHWH* “the branch of YHWH”: *ṣemaḥ* is “sprout, growth,” what springs from the ground (BDB; HALOT; Gen 19:25; Ezek 16:7). In parallel with *pᵉrî hāʾāreṣ* “the fruit of the land,” it most naturally names the restored growth of the land as YHWH’s gift (Wildberger; Williamson; Blenkinsopp). The Targum reads “the Messiah of YHWH,” and Oswalt (*The Book of Isaiah 1–39*, NICOT, 1986) defends the messianic reading. *ṣemaḥ* is a royal title elsewhere: in Jer 23:5; 33:15 it is “a branch for David,” and in Zech 3:8; 6:12 “Branch” is a name (“my servant the Branch,” “a man whose name is Branch”). None of these has the construct *ṣemaḥ YHWH*. The lower-case “branch” keeps the word without deciding for the title (overlay `tsemach-yhwh-branch-isaiah-4`).

The four *lᵉ*-predicates are kept as nouns, “beauty and glory … pride and honor”; ASV turns them into adjectives. *tip̄ʾereṯ* is “honor,” as in the triad “for praise, for fame and for honor” (Deut 26:19; Jer 13:11), so that “splendor” stays with *hāḏār* (2:10, 19, 21) and “glory” with *kāḇôḏ*. *gāʾôn*, used of YHWH’s majesty at 2:10, 19, 21, here names what the land becomes for its people. *pᵉlêṭaṯ yiśrāʾēl* “the survivors of Israel” is the collective sense of *pᵉlêṭāh*, “those who escaped” (2 Kgs 19:30–31 = Isa 37:31–32). The central `pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus` entry is cited, not applied, because its rendering is the event sense “a great deliverance” (Gen 45:7).

paragraphs.translit: bayyōm hahūʾ yihyeh ṣemaḥ YHWH liṣbī ūləkābōd ūpərī hāʾāreṣ ləgāʾōn ūlətipʾeret liplēṭat yiśrāʾēl

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּצִיּ֗וֹן וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קָד֖וֹשׁ יֵאָ֣מֶר ל֑וֹ כָּל־הַכָּת֥וּב לַחַיִּ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

i18n.en: And it shall be that whoever is left in Zion and whoever remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy — everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem —
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּצִיּ֗וֹן וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קָד֖וֹשׁ יֵאָ֣מֶר ל֑וֹ כָּל־הַכָּת֥וּב לַחַיִּ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

notes.official:
*han-nišʾār … wᵉhan-nôṯār* “whoever is left … whoever remains” are participles of *šʾr* and *ytr*, Isaiah’s remnant vocabulary (1:8–9; 6:13; 10:20–22). The central `she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword` entry quotes this verse but governs the noun *šᵉʾērîṯ*; it is cited, not applied. *qāḏôš yēʾāmer lô* “shall be called holy” gives the remnant the root of the title Isaiah gives YHWH, “the Holy One of Israel” (1:4; 5:24).

*kol-hak-kāṯûḇ la-ḥayyîm* may be “written among the living,” the citizen register of Jerusalem (ASV; compare Ezek 13:9; Neh 7:5), or “written for life,” entry in YHWH’s book of the living (NRSV “recorded for life,” NJPS “inscribed for life”; compare Exod 32:32–33; Ps 69:29 [Eng. 28]; Dan 12:1). The Hebrew allows both; the line keeps ASV and the second reading is recorded here (Wildberger; Williamson).

paragraphs.translit: wəhāyāh | hannišʾār bəṣiyyōn wəhannōtār bīrūšālim qādōš yēʾāmer lō kol-hakkātūb laḥayyīm bīrūšālim

paragraphs.text: אִ֣ם ׀ רָחַ֣ץ אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֚ת צֹאַ֣ת בְּנוֹת־צִיּ֔וֹן וְאֶת־דְּמֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָדִ֣יחַ מִקִּרְבָּ֑הּ בְּר֥וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבְר֥וּחַ בָּעֵֽר׃

i18n.en: when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of justice and by a spirit of burning.
i18n.he: אִ֣ם ׀ רָחַ֣ץ אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֚ת צֹאַ֣ת בְּנוֹת־צִיּ֔וֹן וְאֶת־דְּמֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָדִ֣יחַ מִקִּרְבָּ֑הּ בְּר֥וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבְר֥וּחַ בָּעֵֽר׃

notes.official:
*bᵉrûaḥ mišpāṭ û-ḇᵉrûaḥ bāʿēr* “by a spirit of justice and by a spirit of burning”: *rûaḥ* is here the agent of the purge. ASV, NRSV and NJPS all have “spirit”; *rûaḥ* can also be “wind, blast” (HALOT), a sense recorded here and not adopted. The line keeps lower-case “spirit” under the Isaiah house style (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`, extended to this verse). *mišpāṭ* is the judicial act, “justice” (ASV) or “judgment” (KJV, NRSV). *bāʿēr* is “burning” (ASV, NRSV). NJPS has “a spirit of purging,” the sense “remove, purge” (BDB 128–129) of the Deuteronomic formula *ûḇiʿartā hāraʿ* “so you shall purge the evil” (Deut 13:6 [Eng. 5]), and both senses suit the verse, which leads into the fire of v. 5.

*ʾim* is temporal here, “when … has washed away.” *ṣōʾāh* is excrement (Deut 23:14 [Eng. 13]; Isa 28:8); “filth” (ASV, NRSV) softens it. *dᵉmê*, plural, is shed blood, bloodguilt (1:15), rendered “the blood.” *ʾăḏōnāy* is “the Lord” (overlay `adonai-standalone-title-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: ʾim | rāḥaṣ ʾădōnāy ʾēt ṣōʾat bənōt-ṣiyyōn wəʾet-dəmē yərūšālim yādīaḥ miqqirbāh bərūaḥ mišpāṭ ūbərūaḥ bāʿēr

paragraphs.text: וּבָרָ֣א יְהוָ֡ה עַל֩ כָּל־מְכ֨וֹן הַר־צִיּ֜וֹן וְעַל־מִקְרָאֶ֗הָ עָנָ֤ן ׀ יוֹמָם֙ וְעָשָׁ֔ן וְנֹ֛גַהּ אֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה כִּ֥י עַל־כָּל־כָּב֖וֹד חֻפָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there shall be a canopy.
i18n.he: וּבָרָ֣א יְהוָ֡ה עַל֩ כָּל־מְכ֨וֹן הַר־צִיּ֜וֹן וְעַל־מִקְרָאֶ֗הָ עָנָ֤ן ׀ יוֹמָם֙ וְעָשָׁ֔ן וְנֹ֛גַהּ אֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה כִּ֥י עַל־כָּל־כָּב֖וֹד חֻפָּֽה׃

notes.official:
*ʿānān yômām wᵉʿāšān wᵉnōḡah ʾēš lehāḇāh lāylāh* “a cloud by day and smoke, and the shining of a flaming fire by night”: the disjunctive accent (zaqef) on *wᵉʿāšān* closes the first group, so cloud and smoke are the day sign and the fire the night sign; the line follows that division (overlay `anan-chuppah-sukkah-zion-canopy-isaiah-4`). The pairing recalls the wilderness sign, “by day in a pillar of cloud … by night in a pillar of fire” (Exod 13:21–22; Num 9:15–16), and the smoke of Sinai (Exod 19:18). The verse has no *ʿammûḏ* “pillar,” and the line does not supply one. The central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus` entry, whose rationale already treats this verse, now governs it as the Zion redeployment of the Exodus sign (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; Williamson), with its disavowals.

*ûḇārāʾ YHWH* “And YHWH will create”: *bārāʾ* has YHWH alone as subject, and the line has “create” (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`, extended here). The LXX reads *kai hēxei* “and he will come,” as if Hebrew *ûḇāʾ*, and an NJPS footnote records the emendation “spread” (compare Ps 105:39); the line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *mᵉḵôn* “habitation” is the fixed place of YHWH’s dwelling (Exod 15:17; 1 Kgs 8:13). *miqrāʾehā* “her assemblies” are the sacred convocations (Lev 23:2–4); the LXX has “all the places around it.”

*kî ʿal-kol-kāḇôḏ ḥuppāh*: *ḥuppāh* is a canopy or bridal chamber (Joel 2:16; Ps 19:6 [Eng. 5]; HALOT), and the line has “canopy” (NRSV, NJPS) for ASV “covering.” The bare *kāḇôḏ* may be the presence-glory over Zion under the canopy, or the glory itself spread as the canopy (“over everything the glory shall be a canopy”). The line keeps ASV’s construal, “over all the glory.”

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim; claim type: speculative).** The canon does not cite Isa 4:5. *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) reads the pillar of cloud by day and fire by night (Exod 13:21) as the Elohim’s own guidance of Israel (“we guided them,” TBWTT 3:10–11), and the cloud of Exod 14:19 as smoke laid behind the people as a curtain that slowed the pursuers (TBWTT 3:13–14). That is a framework claim of the canon for the Exodus verses. Carrying the reading to the cloud, smoke and fire over Zion is a project synthesis that goes beyond what the canon states, so it is labelled speculative. The line and the glossary carry only the theophany vocabulary.

paragraphs.translit: ūbārāʾ YHWH ʿal kol-məkōn har-ṣiyyōn wəʿal-miqrāʾehā ʿānān | yōmām wəʿāšān wənōgah ʾēš lehābāh lāyəlāh kī ʿal-kol-kābōd ḥuppāh

paragraphs.text: וְסֻכָּ֛ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְצֵל־יוֹמָ֖ם מֵחֹ֑רֶב וּלְמַחְסֶה֙ וּלְמִסְתּ֔וֹר מִזֶּ֖רֶם וּמִמָּטָֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And there shall be a pavilion for a shade by day from the heat, and for a refuge and a shelter from storm and from rain.
i18n.he: וְסֻכָּ֛ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְצֵל־יוֹמָ֖ם מֵחֹ֑רֶב וּלְמַחְסֶה֙ וּלְמִסְתּ֔וֹר מִזֶּ֖רֶם וּמִמָּטָֽר׃ (פ)

notes.official: *sukkāh* is a booth, a temporary shelter of branches (1:8 “a booth in a vineyard”; Lev 23:42). Here the shelter is the divine canopy of v. 5, not a field hut, and the line keeps ASV “pavilion” (NJPS; NRSV “it will serve as a pavilion”). NRSV makes the canopy of v. 5 the subject; the line takes *sukkāh* as the subject of *tihyeh*. *ṣēl* “shade,” *maḥseh* “refuge,” *zerem* “storm” and *ḥōreḇ* “heat” recur together at 25:4, the refuge YHWH is for the poor.

paragraphs.translit: wəsukkāh tihyeh ləṣēl-yōmām mēḥōreb ūləmaḥseh ūləmistōr mizzerem ūmimmāṭār (p)
